summary: Shaded kerb by sports fields near UQ, but a busy feeder road already packed with parked cars.
reasons: Kerb already lined with parked cars by day
Feeds a busy arterial, likely traffic noise

criteria.room: Esri (2025) and QLD (2022) both show this kerb lined almost continuously with parked cars for most of its 276 m, consistent with heavy daytime demand near UQ sportsgrounds and a school. No clear long gap visible in either image; whether space frees up overnight can't be judged from daytime imagery.
criteria.frontage: Faces open recreation land - tennis courts (chunk 1) and bowling greens (chunk 2) - not houses. Across the 3-lane road are houses/units and, further south, a school or childcare complex with shade sails and a large carpark.
criteria.overlooked: No windows look directly onto the kerb itself; it's screened by trees and backs onto sportsground. Houses sit on the far side of the road, set back behind footpaths, so overlook is low.
criteria.slope: Mean grade 2.6%, uneven along the length: near-flat (~0.1% over 20 m) at the north end by the Sir Fred Schonell Drive intersection, rising to a steep hump (max 11.2%) around two-thirds down, easing again near the southern bend. The flat northern ~100 m (chunk 1) is the best place to park.
criteria.disturbance: North end sits right at Sir Fred Schonell Drive, a signed traffic-control area with weekday peak clearways - busier at peak times, likely quiet at night. Keith St carries 3 lanes at 50 km/h with repeated 'No Stopping Any Time' signage, suggesting more through-traffic than a typical quiet residential street. A nearby school may add drop-off/pick-up noise on weekday mornings/afternoons, not overnight.
criteria.shade: Continuous mature tree canopy overhangs most of the kerb in both images - good shade, but dense overhanging branches could drop sap or debris on a van.
criteria.signs_vs_imagery: OSM tags this stretch 'parking:both: no', but imagery clearly shows cars parked continuously along the kerb in both 2022 and 2025 captures, so parking is evidently used/tolerated here, consistent with the 'P (No Limit)' signs rather than the OSM tag.

cannot_judge: Whether the daytime parking crowding clears overnight
Real traffic volume/noise at night vs daytime appearance
